A new artificial intelligence model, DeepFAN, was validated in China’s first multi-center clinical trial for pulmonary nodule assessment. It demonstrated high accuracy and, when used as an assistant, substantially improved junior radiologists’ diagnostic accuracy, confidence and consistency in distinguishing malignant nodules from benign ones.

References
Gould, M. K. et al. Recent trends in the identification of incidental pulmonary nodules. Am. J. Resp. Crit. Care Med. 192, 1208–1214 (2015). This study found that the increased use of chest CT imaging led to a substantially higher identification rate of incidental pulmonary nodules.
Ng, A. Y. et al. Prospective implementation of AI-assisted screen reading to improve early detection of breast cancer. Nat. Med. 29, 3044–3049 (2023). This paper validated AI’s role as an independent second reader to improve early detection of breast cancer in a real-world screening setting.
Wang, Y. W. et al. Proposing a deep learning-based method for improving the diagnostic certainty of pulmonary nodules in CT scan of chest. Eur. Radiol. 31, 8160–8167 (2021). This article reported that an AI model can reduce diagnostic uncertainty in the classification of pulmonary nodules.
Poterucha, T. J. et al. Detecting structural heart disease from electrocardiograms using AI. Nature 644, 221–230 (2025). In this study, an AI model demonstrated the ability to detect structural heart disease by simultaneously improving both diagnostic sensitivity and diagnostic specificity.
